chapter: New Orleans bands, players and halls
title: Older bass players: Kimball, Glennie and John Prudence
summary: Foster rates Kimball one of the best old bassists; the interviewer relays Glennie's remembering John Prudence as the first to pick bass.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: I was going to ask about some more of the older bass players, if you remember them, like Kimball.
Well, I used to regard Kimball, well, I regard Kimball as one of the best bass players we had down there. I regard him as that. He was older than you,
Oh, yeah. Kimball's son was almost older than me.
I once asked old man Glennie.
He had a daughter, older than his son.

I once asked Mr. Glennie who was the first player he ever heard pick the bass, or if he was, or who was, and he said he, first one he heard was a fellow by the name of Prudence. How do you pronounce it fast? John Prudence.
Well, I didn't know, see, when I was home in 45, Glennie then was around 86 or 90, something then.
And Waken, Plaston. That was a solid old man, wasn't he?
